title: Render aggregate living-report presentation on the Report cover
description:
The living-report service publishes a specialized aggregate status block, but the Report cover omits the block reference, so operators see only the legacy prose projection.

Feature: Living-report aggregate presentation

Scenario: Open a published living optimization Report
  Given the Report has a published OptimizationRunStatus block
  And that block points to a verified stakeholder-presentation artifact
  When an operator opens the Report detail view
  Then the Report cover renders the aggregate optimization presentation
  And the compact prose remains available as supporting context

Scenario: Open the Report before aggregate evidence exists
  Given the Report status block exists but its first presentation revision is not yet available
  When an operator opens the Report detail view
  Then the cover presents an honest loading or unavailable state
  And it does not invent aggregate findings

Out of scope:
- New GraphQL models or infrastructure resources.
- Changing the immutable artifact contract.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Dogfood reproduced the defect against a fresh production-backed Report: the specialized status block and immutable presentation descriptor were present, but the cover rendered only prose because it omitted the normal report-block code fence. Added the cover reference plus a dashboard ReportTask integration specification. Validation is green: 46 focused Python tests, 11 dashboard tests, and TypeScript compilation. No schema or infrastructure resources changed. The bounded test run completed in 4m44s with zero model cost and no operational mutations.
